_why: Checklist lines the rebuilt lessons still omit (2026 Division B Experimental Design Checklist, soinc.org), plus event rules 3.b-3.c and 4.d-4.g.

independent-and-dependent: The checklist scores 'IV correctly identified and operationally defined' and 'DV correctly identified and operationally defined' (3 points each). Teach what an operational definition is — stating exactly how the variable is changed or measured, with units and instrument (e.g. 'flight time measured with a stopwatch to the nearest hundredth of a second', as in the official CER guide) — and show one for an IV and one for a DV.
experimental-error: The checklist scores each of two errors as '1st/2nd specific error is identified & effect on results discussed' (3 points each). Teach that naming an error is not enough: state how that error would change the measured results (which direction, which levels of the IV).
safety-in-the-design: Rules 4.d-4.g: a participant not following proper safety procedures is asked to leave and the team is disqualified from the event; not following clean-up procedures multiplies the final score by 0.95; not addressing the assigned question multiplies it by up to 0.75; not collecting data on site or making up data multiplies it by 0.25. Goggles are required (rule 2.a). State these consequences explicitly.
time-budget: Rules 3.b-3.c: in the first 20 minutes teams receive the question, materials and Part I of the report form and focus on designing and conducting the experiment; after 20 minutes they receive Part II and focus on analysis and reporting, and may keep experimenting for the whole ~50-minute event. Build the time budget on those two phases.

Do not claim that repeated trials automatically make an experiment valid: repetition reduces the effect of random error and shows variation, but it cannot fix a systematic error or a confounded design.
reading-a-trend: The official CER guide states the line-of-best-fit slope as 0.80 s/paperclip, but a least-squares fit to the means it tabulates (0, 1, 2, 3 paperclips: 3.43, 5.17, 5.12, 6.63 s) gives about 0.96 s per paperclip. Do not state 0.80 next to those means. Either show the calculation from the data in the lesson (slope ~0.96 s per paperclip, positive) or say only that the slope is positive.
